column1: How is the scalar alignment score $e_{t,i}$ computed in Bahdanau additive attention?
column2: It is calculated using a learnable feed-forward network (MLP) evaluated on the previous decoder state $s_{t-1}$ and encoder hidden state $h_i$: $e_{t,i} = f_{\text{att}}(s_{t-1}, h_i)$.

column1: What structural challenge in processing high-resolution images with Vision Transformers was specifically addressed by the Swin Transformer?
column2: The quadratic computational complexity $O(N^2)$ of global self-attention across large numbers of fine-grained pixel patches, solved using local shifted windows and patch merging.

column1: How do per-layer computational complexities compare between RNNs and Self-Attention for sequence length $N$ and embedding dimension $d$?
column2: RNN per-layer complexity is $O(N \cdot d^2)$, whereas Self-Attention per-layer complexity is $O(N^2 \cdot d)$.

column1: What two main functional sub-layers make up a standard Transformer encoder block?
column2:
1. Multi-Head Self-Attention
2. Position-wise Feed-Forward Neural Network (MLP applied independently to each token position).

column1: What two architectural elements wrap around each sub-layer in a Transformer block to enable gradient flow in deep networks?
column2: Residual (skip) connections and Layer Normalization.

column1: What is the primary function of masked (causal) self-attention in a Transformer decoder?
column2: To prevent decoder token representations at position $i$ from attending to future tokens ($j > i$) during autoregressive generation.

column1: In sinusoidal positional encodings, how does frequency vary across embedding dimensions $k$?
column2: The angular velocity $W_k = \frac{1}{10000^{2k/d}}$ decreases exponentially with dimension index $k$, giving low dimensions high frequencies (short periods) and high dimensions low frequencies (long periods).

column1: How is the dynamic context vector $c_t$ calculated at decoder step $t$ in an attention-augmented sequence model?
column2: As a weighted sum of all encoder hidden states $h_i$ scaled by their respective attention weights $a_{t,i}$: $c_t = \sum_i a_{t,i} h_i$.

column1: In sequence processing architectures shown below: Diagram illustrating sequence processing configurations: one to one, one to many, many to one, delayed many to many, and synced many to many. Which configuration represents traditional Encoder-Decoder sequence-to-sequence machine translation?
column2: The fourth diagram: Many-to-Many with a delayed output sequence (reading the entire input sequence before decoding starts).

column1: What is the maximum path length between any two tokens in a sequence of length $N$ for RNNs versus Transformers?
column2: RNNs require $O(N)$ sequential operations to traverse hidden states, whereas Transformers achieve an $O(1)$ constant path length due to direct all-to-all attention connections.

column1: In visual attention models for image captioning (e.g., Show, Attend and Tell), what represents the input over which attention is computed?
column2: A grid of spatial feature vectors $z_{i,j} \in \mathbb{R}^D$ extracted from intermediate convolutional layers of a CNN.

column1: How do Queries ($Q$), Keys ($K$), and Values ($V$) differ between self-attention and cross-attention in a Transformer decoder?
column2: In self-attention, $Q, K, V$ all originate from the decoder sequence. In cross-attention, $Q$ comes from the decoder while $K$ and $V$ originate from the encoder output.

column1: How is causal masking implemented in the self-attention alignment score matrix?
column2: Alignment scores corresponding to future token positions ($j > i$) are set to $-\infty$, forcing their post-softmax attention weights to zero.

column1: What primary bottleneck occurs in standard sequence-to-sequence Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) models when handling long input sequences?
column2: The entire input sequence must be compressed into a single fixed-size context vector $c$, causing severe information loss for long sequences (e.g., $T \ge 1000$).

column1: How is the updated output representation $y_i$ computed for token position $i$ in a self-attention layer?
column2: As a weighted sum of all Value vectors $v_j$ weighted by the softmax-normalized attention scores $a_{i,j}$: $y_i = \sum_j a_{i,j} v_j$.

column1: What is the primary motivation for using Multi-Head Attention instead of single-head self-attention?
column2: It allows the model to simultaneously attend to information from different representation subspaces and structural relationships at different sequence positions.

column1: What four core properties must an effective positional encoding function satisfy?
column2:
1. Produce a unique encoding for each time-step position.
2. Ensure distance between any two steps is consistent across sequence lengths.
3. Generalize deterministically to longer sequences.
4. Produce bounded values.

column1: In the Query-Key-Value ($QKV$) framework of self-attention, how are $q_i$, $k_i$, and $v_i$ obtained from an input vector $x_i$?
column2: By multiplying $x_i$ by three separate learned projection matrices: $q_i = W_Q x_i$, $k_i = W_K x_i$, and $v_i = W_V x_i$.

column1: How does a Vision Transformer (ViT) format a 2D image into a sequence compatible with a standard Transformer encoder?
column2: It divides the image into non-overlapping spatial patches (e.g., $16 \times 16$ pixels), flattens each patch into a vector, and linearly projects them into token embeddings.

column1: Why does the Bahdanau attention mechanism require no explicit ground-truth supervision of attention weights during training?
column2: Because all steps (alignment score MLP, softmax, and weighted sum) are fully differentiable, allowing backpropagation end-to-end directly from the output loss.

column1: Over what dimensions are visual attention weights normalized when generating each word in image captioning?
column2: Normalized using softmax across all spatial grid locations $(i,j)$ of the feature map, ensuring $\sum_{i,j} a_{t,i,j} = 1$.

column1: What is the formula for scaled dot-product similarity between Query $q_i$ and Key $k_j$ in self-attention?
column2: $e_{i,j} = \frac{q_i \cdot k_j}{\sqrt{d_k}}$, where $d_k$ is the dimensionality of the Key vectors.

column1: Why is standard self-attention inherently permutation-equivariant with respect to input tokens?
column2: Because dot-product comparisons compare input token vectors set-wise without any inherent notion of word order or sequence index.

column1: How do Vision Transformers (ViTs) contrast with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in terms of inductive bias?
column2: CNNs have built-in inductive biases for spatial locality and translation equivariance, while ViTs have minimal inductive bias, enabling them to learn global patterns when trained on massive datasets.

column1: What mathematical function normalizes raw alignment scores $e_{t,i}$ into attention weights $a_{t,i}$ across input positions $i$?
column2: The softmax function: $a_{t,i} = \frac{\exp(e_{t,i})}{\sum_k \exp(e_{t,k})}$, ensuring $0 < a_{t,i} < 1$ and $\sum_i a_{t,i} = 1$.

column1: Why must positional encodings be added to input token embeddings in Transformer networks?
column2: To inject word order and relative token placement information into the self-attention mechanism, which is otherwise order-agnostic.

column1: Why are Transformer encoder layers significantly easier to parallelize during training compared to RNN layers?
column2: Because self-attention processes all sequence tokens simultaneously ($O(1)$ sequential operations per layer), unlike RNNs which require sequential step-by-step unrolling ($O(N)$ sequential steps).
